topic: Interactions in Estuaries and Intertidal Zones
key_concepts: Estuaries form where river freshwater meets ocean saltwater and have brackish water.
Estuaries are called nurseries of the seas because many organisms reproduce there.
Estuaries filter sediments and pollutants and serve as flood exit points.
Intertidal zones are coastal areas exposed to rising and receding tides.
Waves, salinity, temperature, sunlight, and soil type are abiotic factors in these habitat
Mangroves and blue crabs are adapted to changing salinity.
Shallow estuary and intertidal waters allow sunlight for photosynthesis by algae, seaweeds
Soil type affects which living things live in these ecosystems.
Living things interact through feeding relationships that cycle nutrients and energy.
